manuscript_claim: Outcome truncation induced by action-dependent observation can substantially distort measured calibration.
support2_evidence: Strong empirical support using linked 60-day outcomes.
mimic_evidence: Strong empirical support using linked 30-day outcomes.
permitted_language: Action-dependent outcome truncation substantially changed measured calibration in both clinical datasets.
prohibited_language: Do not describe the distortion as a causal treatment effect.

manuscript_claim: Calibration distortion is heterogeneous across risk, observation pathways, clinical subgroups, care settings, and time.
support2_evidence: Supported across DNR, disease, and hospital-timing partitions.
mimic_evidence: Supported across ICU status, era, time of admission, disease chapter, service, admission type, and admission location; weekend effects were not supported.
permitted_language: The magnitude of distortion varied meaningfully across prespecified and descriptive strata.
prohibited_language: Do not interpret subgroup contrasts as causal effects. Do not claim an institution effect because institution identifiers were unavailable.

manuscript_claim: Adjustment performance depends on identification and overlap; greater model flexibility alone does not guarantee recovery of linked calibration.
synthetic_evidence: Strong support under controlled identified and non-identified regimes.
support2_evidence: Survival outcome regression substantially reduced error and performed best.
mimic_evidence: Score-only, rich logistic, HGB, RF, IPCW, and augmented estimators remained materially separated from the linked reference; RF-AIPW gave partial reduction only.
permitted_language: Adjustment succeeded in the better-identified SUPPORT2 setting but not under the severe MIMIC positivity limitations.
prohibited_language: Do not claim that all adjustment methods fail universally or that survival regression always succeeds.

manuscript_claim: Localized action- or stratum-specific sensitivity analysis reveals heterogeneous robustness that can be obscured by a common global perturbation.
synthetic_evidence: Sensitivity model validated under controlled conditions.
support2_evidence: Descriptive discharge-linked partitions reduced the closest robustness margin by up to 41.8%.
mimic_evidence: Native discharge-action analysis reduced the closest robustness margin by 76.3%; hospice was closest to tipping.
permitted_language: Localized sensitivity provided information hidden by a single global perturbation.
prohibited_language: Do not describe SUPPORT2 DNR, disease, or timing partitions as native causal actions.

manuscript_claim: Changes in observation policy can generate substantial apparent calibration drift despite an unchanged predictor, population, and complete-outcome target.
support2_evidence: Aggressive policy increased restricted ICI while the reference target remained fixed; the conservative contrast was inconclusive.
mimic_evidence: Aggressive policy increased restricted ICI and conservative policy decreased it while reference quantities remained fixed.
permitted_language: Observation-policy shifts produced apparent drift in controlled real-data-grounded emulations.
prohibited_language: Do not describe the emulations as historical or causal estimates of actual hospital policy changes.

manuscript_claim: Recalibration fitted on policy-selected observed outcomes can improve the restricted target while harming the unchanged complete-population target, but this behavior is dataset- and policy-dependent rather than universal.
support2_evidence: Not replicated: aggressive logistic recalibration worsened ICI on both the restricted and reference targets.
mimic_evidence: Strong support: aggressive logistic recalibration improved restricted ICI and log loss while worsening both reference metrics.
final_status: bounded support with explicit dataset-specific non-replication
permitted_language: Policy-selected recalibration can create target mismatch, as observed in synthetic data and MIMIC.
prohibited_language: Do not describe H7 as strong cross-dataset support or as a universal failure of recalibration.
